what_it_does.name: skill-creator
what_it_does.summary: Instructions, three subagent prompts, a JSON schema reference and Python scripts for creating agent skills and improving them in a loop. The workflow captures what the skill should do, drafts a SKILL.md, runs test prompts with and without the skill in subagents, grades and aggregates the runs into a benchmark, and shows outputs and benchmark in a browser viewer where the user leaves feedback. A separate loop tests the description against realistic trigger queries through claude -p and proposes better descriptions, and a packager zips the finished skill into a .skill file. Use it to create a skill from scratch, edit or optimize an existing skill, run evals or improve triggering.
tasks: capture intent and draft a new SKILL.md
run test prompts with and without the skill in subagents
grade runs and aggregate a benchmark with mean and stddev
review outputs and leave feedback in a browser eval viewer
optimize the description for triggering accuracy
package a skill as a .skill file

checks.tool: Snyk, skills.sh audit, version not stated
checks.result: pass, risk level LOW, no issues detected

checks.tool: Gen Agent Trust Hub, skills.sh audit, version not stated
checks.scope: the scripts, the eval viewer and the instructions, as cited in its analysis
checks.result: pass, risk level SAFE, four surfaces described, claude CLI subprocess calls, a local server on 127.0.0.1, an indirect prompt injection surface and SheetJS loaded from a CDN

checks.tool: Socket, skills.sh audit, version not stated
checks.result: warn, 1 alert, Anomaly LOW in eval-viewer/viewer.html, DOM XSS potential and unsandboxed iframe data URIs, confidence 55%, severity 68%

vulnerabilities.finding: Anomaly, DOM XSS potential through container.innerHTML fed from EMBEDDED_DATA and iframe.src set to file.data_uri without sandboxing
vulnerabilities.fix: review for strict escaping, URI validation and safe rendering or sandboxing

risks.risk: Instructions hidden in user inputs, run outputs or transcripts reach the agent, since the skill reads and grades content it did not write.
risks.mitigation: the instructions forbid creating malicious skills, per C2, no delimiting of read content is stated

risks.risk: A crafted output file or eval data shown in the eval viewer could run script in the browser, since innerHTML and iframe src take embedded data without full escaping or sandboxing.
Trigger evals and description improvement start claude -p subprocesses with the user's environment and session auth, up to 10 in parallel by default.
risks.mitigation: argument lists are used against command injection, per C2, in place

risks.risk: A changed copy of SheetJS on the CDN would run in the viewer page.
risks.mitigation: the script tag carries a sha384 integrity hash, in place

risks.risk: Starting the viewer ends any other process already listening on port 3117, since generate_review.py sends it SIGTERM without asking.
risks.mitigation: none stated, the --static option writes a file instead of starting a server

limitations: Description optimization needs the claude CLI, which is only available in Claude Code, so it is skipped on Claude.ai.
Without subagents, as on Claude.ai, test cases run one at a time without baselines and quantitative benchmarking is skipped.
Simple one-step queries may not trigger a skill even when the description matches, so trigger evals need substantive queries.
Timing data comes only through the task notification and is not persisted elsewhere.
Without a display the viewer cannot open a browser, so it is written as a static HTML file and feedback is downloaded as feedback.json.
Packaging and presenting happen only if the present_files tool is available.
The installed skill path may be read-only, so a copy is edited in /tmp/.
Descriptions over 1024 characters are truncated, and quick_validate.py rejects descriptions with angle brackets.
No dependency except SheetJS carries a version.

known_problems.problem: Cowork disinclines Claude from generating the eval viewer after running the tests
known_problems.workaround: generate the viewer with generate_review.py before evaluating outputs yourself
run the test prompts in series rather than parallel

known_problems.problem: the viewer shows empty or zero values
known_problems.workaround: use the exact field names text, passed, evidence and configuration from references/schemas.md

known_problems.problem: the viewer port is still in use
known_problems.workaround: generate_review.py kills the process on the port or picks a free port

known_problems.problem: a proposed description is over 1024 characters
known_problems.workaround: one more call asks for a rewrite under the limit

known_problems.problem: direct writes may fail due to permissions when packaging
known_problems.workaround: stage in /tmp/ first, then copy to the output directory

known_problems.problem: several exported eval sets in Downloads
known_problems.workaround: use the most recent, for instance eval_set (1).json
